summary_hint: Closing wire instructions from <issuing_firm_name>: beneficiary <beneficiary_name> at <bank_name> (routing/account masked).

typed_core.name: beneficiary_name
typed_core.why: identity — who receives the wire (the title/law-firm/escrow account holder)
typed_core.prompt_hint: The full beneficiary line, including any 'c/o' — unmasked

typed_core.name: aba_routing_number
typed_core.why: PII — the receiving bank's ABA/wire routing number (9 digits; masked at the snapshot boundary)
typed_core.prompt_hint: The wire/ABA routing number as printed; captured verbatim, masked + hashed at the snapshot boundary

typed_core.name: account_number
typed_core.why: PII — the beneficiary account number the funds go to (masked at the snapshot boundary)
typed_core.prompt_hint: The account number as printed; captured verbatim, masked + hashed at the snapshot boundary

typed_core.name: account_type
typed_core.why: processor — the account type when stated (e.g. IOLTA trust account)

typed_core.name: verification_phone
typed_core.why: processor — the callback phone to VERIFY the instructions (anti-wire-fraud); a processor must read it, so it stays UNMASKED
typed_core.prompt_hint: The verification/callback phone as printed, KEEPING its formatting (parentheses/dashes) — do not strip to bare digits

typed_core.name: reference_or_memo
typed_core.why: processor — what to reference on the wire (borrower name / property / file number)

typed_core.name: issuing_firm_name
typed_core.why: identity — the firm that issued the instructions (title company / law firm / escrow agent)

typed_core.name: document_date
typed_core.why: processor — the date on the instructions, when printed (recency / anti-fraud freshness)
typed_core.prompt_hint: Only if a date is printed; leave null otherwise (154 has none)

rejected.name: is_verified / looks_fraudulent / is_trusted
rejected.reason: JUDGMENTS, not facts — whether the instructions are verified/legitimate is a processor's anti-fraud action, not a value on the page. The type EXISTS to surface the fields (masked) so a processor can verify; it must not pre-judge. Tags describe; rules judge.

rejected.name: wire_amount
rejected.reason: a wire-instructions sheet is a PAYEE sheet (where to send), not an amount; the closing amount lives on the CD. Capturing an 'amount' here invites a false match and is not reliably printed.

rejected.name: swift_or_intermediary_bank
rejected.reason: domestic closing wires rarely carry SWIFT/intermediary detail; when present it is contact/routing minutiae — catch-all

encoding_variations: issued by a title company, law firm (IOLTA trust account), or escrow/settlement agent — issuing_firm_name + account_type vary accordingly
the routing number is 9 digits; the account number is longer — both are bare contiguous digit runs that trip the LP-209 at-rest guard and MUST be masked (registered in _PII_FIELDS)
verification_phone is usually formatted ((877) 838-0777) — kept unmasked and formatting-preserved so it does not become a bare 10-digit run
reference_or_memo may embed a file/loan number — scrubbed at the snapshot boundary as a belt-and-braces backstop

open_questions.recommendation: UNMASKED (GEET'S DECISION, LP-466): it is the anti-fraud callback a processor must read; a formatted phone does not trip the contiguous-digit at-rest guard

notes: The reason for the type is PII HANDLING, not a rule (rules_served empty). These currently land in general_correspondence — free-form and UNMASKED. Typed + masked (aba_routing_number, account_number) beats free-form.
aba_routing_number is a NEW _PII_FIELDS registration (ACCOUNT, from_raw); account_number is already registered globally (reuse).
reference_or_memo is added to _SCRUB_FREE_TEXT_FIELDS for wire_instructions (the 9+-digit backstop) in case a memo embeds a bare file/loan number.
